### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/dp/dp_display.c`**
   - The patch reverts a previous change that used `drm_bridge_hpd_notify()` to report Hot Plug Detect (HPD) status changes.
   - A new function `dp_display_send_hpd_event()` is introduced, which sends HPD events using `drm_helper_hpd_irq_event()` instead of the previously used method.
   - The `dp_display_send_hpd_notification()` function is modified to call the new `dp_display_send_hpd_event()` function instead of `drm_bridge_hpd_notify()`. This change ensures that HPD notifications are sent correctly based on the current state of the link.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The primary relationship is that the new function `dp_display_send_hpd_event()` is designed to replace the functionality of `drm_bridge_hpd_notify()`, which was causing issues in the driver’s state machine and leading to delays or failures in detecting display connections.
- The revert of the previous commit (e467e0bde881) indicates that the changes made in that commit were problematic, prompting the introduction of a new method for handling HPD events that aims to restore proper functionality while a more comprehensive fix is being developed.

Here is the commit message:
Revert "drm/msm/dp: use drm_bridge_hpd_notify() to report HPD
 status changes"

This reverts commit e467e0bde881 ("drm/msm/dp: use
drm_bridge_hpd_notify() to report HPD status changes").

The commit changed the way how the MSM DP driver communicates
HPD-related events to the userspace. The mentioned commit made some of
the HPD events being reported earlier. This way userspace starts poking
around. It interacts in a bad way with the dp_bridge_detect and the
driver's state machine, ending up either with the very long delays
during hotplug detection or even inability of the DP driver to report
the display as connected.

A proper fix will involve redesigning of the HPD handling in the MSM DP
driver. It is underway, but it will be intrusive and can not be thought
about as a simple fix for the issue. Thus, revert the offending commit.

Fixes: e467e0bde881 ("drm/msm/dp: use drm_bridge_hpd_notify() to report HPD status changes")
Link: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/msm/-/issues/50
Reported-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/Zd3YPGmrprxv-N-O@hovoldconsulting.com/

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240227220808.50146-1-dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the change in how the MSM DP driver communicated HPD-related events to userspace. The previous implementation using `drm_bridge_hpd_notify()` led to premature reporting of HPD events, which interfered with the `dp_bridge_detect` function and the driver's state machine. This resulted in long delays during hotplug detection and, in some cases, the inability of the DP driver to correctly report the display as connected.

Here is the patch:
 
+static void dp_display_send_hpd_event(struct msm_dp *dp_display)
+{
+	struct dp_display_private *dp;
+	struct drm_connector *connector;
+
+	dp = container_of(dp_display, struct dp_display_private, dp_display);
+
+	connector = dp->dp_display.connector;
+	drm_helper_hpd_irq_event(connector->dev);
+}
+
 static int dp_display_send_hpd_notification(struct dp_display_private *dp,
 					    bool hpd)
 {
-	struct drm_bridge *bridge = dp->dp_display.bridge;
+	if ((hpd && dp->dp_display.link_ready) ||
+			(!hpd && !dp->dp_display.link_ready)) {
+		drm_dbg_dp(dp->drm_dev, "HPD already %s\n",
+				(hpd ? "on" : "off"));
+		return 0;
+	}
 
 	/* reset video pattern flag on disconnect */
 	if (!hpd) {
 		dp->panel->video_test = false;
 		if (!dp->dp_display.is_edp)
 			drm_dp_set_subconnector_property(dp->dp_display.connector,
 							 connector_status_disconnected,
 							 dp->panel->dpcd,
 							 dp->panel->downstream_ports);
 	}
 
 	dp->dp_display.link_ready = hpd;
 
 	drm_dbg_dp(dp->drm_dev, "type=%d hpd=%d\n",
 			dp->dp_display.connector_type, hpd);
-	drm_bridge_hpd_notify(bridge, dp->dp_display.link_ready);
+	dp_display_send_hpd_event(&dp->dp_display);
 
 	return 0;
 }
